title: PipeLink: A Pipelined Resource Sharing System for Dataflow High-Level Synthesis
problem: Dynamically scheduled HLS produces pipelined dataflow circuits, but coordinating pipelined function calls and shared resources is difficult without centralized control, limiting support for general software programs.
motivation: Asynchronous dataflow circuits enable automatic pipelining but lack centralized sequencing, making it hard to pipeline access to shared functions—a critical bottleneck for HLS productivity.
method: PipeLink decomposes synthesis into compilation and linking stages, enabling fully-pipelined access to shared functions in asynchronous dataflow circuits. Uses asynchronous design principles for both pipelined function units and pipelined memory access in a unified framework.
key_novelty: First modular HLS approach combining compilation/linking stages to achieve full pipelining of shared resources in asynchronous dataflow.
contributions: Enables pipelined access to shared function units without centralized control
Unified treatment of pipelined function and memory access
20x energy reduction and 1.56x throughput improvement vs. existing HLS tools
limitations: Not discussed; scalability to complex shared resources and memory hierarchies unclear.
primary_theme: Asynchronous dataflow HLS with pipelined resource sharing
